C08-M08-L04-F1.title: Order of volatility applied to WS-104
C08-M08-L04-F1.caption: Evidence layers from most to least volatile (after RFC 3227), with what each holds in the Banyan incident.
C08-M08-L04-F1.alt: Stack of six layers, most volatile at the top. 1, red: CPU registers and cache, nanoseconds; only by specialist tools. 2, red: Memory, processes, network connections, lost at power-off: decoded PowerShell, beacon config. 3, orange: Temporary file systems, lost at reboot or clean-up. 4, orange: Disk, invoice.docm, svc_update profile, local logs. 5, blue: Remote logs: SIEM, proxy, VPN, durable but subject to retention. 6, slate: Archives and backups, longest-lived.

layers.label: Memory, processes, network connections
layers.sub: lost at power-off: decoded PowerShell, beacon config

C08-M08-L04-F1.note: Collect from the top down; isolation keeps every layer, power-off destroys the red ones.

C08-M08-L04-F2.title: Integrity chain for exported log evidence
C08-M08-L04-F2.caption: How evidence_export.py makes the WS-104 export reproducible, tamper-evident and accountable, and how it is re-verified at every use.
C08-M08-L04-F2.alt: Top-to-bottom flow of six steps. 1, violet: Documented query, host WS-104, 06:00Z-09:00Z, raw events. 2, blue: Raw export, WS-104_2026-11-03_events.jsonl, 32 events. 3, orange: SHA-256 digest, 8521c97c...19acf. 4, green: Manifest + custody entry, SHA256SUMS; custody.jsonl: who, when, query. 5, slate: Store and transfer, restricted or write-once storage; log every hand-over. 6, dark: Re-hash and compare, OK = unchanged; FAILED = altered copy. A dashed loop arrow labelled every hand-over and every use runs from step 6 back to step 5.

steps.label: Store and transfer
steps.sub: restricted or write-once storage; log every hand-over

C08-M08-L04-F2.note: Each link answers a different challenge: reproducibility, integrity, accountability.
